metadata.label: False color
metadata.coverage: Valid infrared/green/violet observations over the observed monochrome base. Gray grid only where neither source has imagery.

science.label: Elevation
science.title: Released relative heights of Agenor Linea; independent local stereo datum, not elevation above a global reference sphere.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic. Source resolution varies from about 200 m to 20 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Original image shading remains; globe lighting is approximate.

controls.label: False color
controls.notes: Galileo false color: 756 nm → red, 559 nm → green, 404 nm → blue, at 1.4–1.6 km per pixel. Color covers part of the surface. A correction for each observation reduces broad photographed shading; oblique views retain observed monochrome. Overall brightness is matched to the monochrome base, preserving linear band ratios. This is not a human-visible color reconstruction. Photographed shadows and seams can remain; added globe lighting is approximate. Gray grid marks gaps in both sources.

controls.label: Elevation

facts.label: Source precision
facts.value: Nominal 52 m; approximately 100 m empirical estimate, not a pointwise error bound

controls.notes: Agenor Linea only, near 142°E and 44°S. Colors encode the released local stereo heights in meters; their relative datum is not a global reference level. Effective detail is about 3 km. Fixed northwest cartographic relief shows slopes; it is not part of the numeric scale. Gray grid preserves the DTM’s finite/no-data footprint. The archive’s duplicated, cubic-resampled quality products are excluded; colors imply no quality class or pointwise accuracy.

controls.label: Geology
controls.notes: USGS interpreted regional plains, bands, chaos terrains and crater deposits (2024; 1:15,000,000). Colors identify map units, not measured surface color. Gray grid marks no-data polygons. Fine line and point features are not represented by this polygon view.

controls.label: Infrared
controls.notes: Galileo NIMS observations assign red, green and blue to 1.50, 1.34 and 0.73–0.74 µm, following the archive guide. This false-color view shows spectral differences, not natural color or mineral abundance. The observations have Minnaert photometric correction; resolution, residual brightness and seams vary. Fixed channel stretches clip extreme values. Gray grid marks areas lacking a valid sample in any selected band.
